arxiv-2407-20049.title: Systematic study of complete fusion suppression for 6,7 Li nuclei using artificial neural network
arxiv-2407-20049.creator: D. Chattopadhyay 1
arxiv-2407-20049.description: Abstract In recent decades, there has been a significant increase in the measurement of complete fusion cross-sections for various reactions, with particular emphasis on the reactions involving weakly bound projectile. It has been well established that the complete fusion cross-section involving weakly bound nuclei is suppressed at above barrier energies due to the breakup effect.

arxiv-2511-07381.title: Residual Rotation Correction using Tactile Equivariance
arxiv-2511-07381.creator: Yizhe Zhu, Zhang Ye, Boce Hu, Haibo Zhao, Yu Qi, Dian Wang, Robert Platt
arxiv-2511-07381.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yizhe Zhu, Zhang Ye, Boce Hu, Haibo Zhao, Yu Qi, Dian Wang, Robert Platt. Visuotactile policy learning augments vision-only policies with tactile input, facilitating contact-rich manipulation. However, the high cost of tactile data collection makes sample efficiency the key requirement for developing visuotactile policies. We present EquiTac, a framework that exploits the inherent SO ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SO}(2) symmetry of in-hand object rotation to improve sample efficiency and generalization for visuotactile policy learning.

pmc-10532208.title: P10 Collapse, confusion and acute kidney injury presenting in the context of bullous skin disease in a young male patient
pmc-10532208.creator: Deepak Nagra, Christopher Baldwin, Jonathan Dick, James Galloway, Aveen Connolly, Chris Wincup
pmc-10532208.description: IntroductionCutaneous manifestations of systemic erythematous lupus (SLE) are common and reported to be present in 75-80% of patients at some point during the course of their illness. Further, lupus-related skin conditions can be the presenting symptom of the disease in a quarter of cases. Bullous skin changes are reported in SLE but are rare, affecting fewer than 5% of patients.

pmc-10610384.title: LipL41 and LigA/LigB Gene Silencing on a LipL32 Knockout Leptospira interrogans Reveals the Impact of Multiple Mutations on Virulence
pmc-10610384.creator: Luis Guilherme V Fernandes, Bruno B Foltran, Aline F Teixeira, Ana Lucia Tabet Oller Nascimento, Bart C Weimer
pmc-10610384.description: Leptospirosis is a global zoonosis caused by pathogenic bacteria of the genus Leptospira. The application of the CRISPR/Cas9 system has facilitated the generation of mutants and subsequent evaluation of phenotypes. Since DNA breaks induced by RNA-guided Cas9 nuclease are lethal to Leptospira, different methodologies were implemented to overcome this limitation.

pmc-11494192.title: Power electronics for green hydrogen generation with focus on methods, topologies, and comparative analysis
pmc-11494192.creator: AlAmir Hassan, Omar Abdel-Rahim, Mohit Bajaj, Ievgen Zaitsev
pmc-11494192.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This research article meticulously examines advanced power electronic converters crucial for optimizing electrolyzer perfor- mance in hydrogen production systems. It conducts a thorough review of mature electrolyzer types, detailing their specifications, electric models, manufacturers, and scalability. To meet the high current and stable DC voltage demands of industrial electrolyzers, the study delves into a broad spectrum of AC-DC and DC-DC converter topologies.

pmc-11771747.title: Perfil de Derivación de Pacientes Adultos Atendidos en la Consulta de Neuropsicología del Hospital Universitario la Paz de Madrid Entre 2018 y 2023
pmc-11771747.creator: Julia Castellanos Segado, Cristina Campoy Lacasa, Diego Carracedo Sanchidrián, Jesús Martí Esquitino
pmc-11771747.description: Introducción:La neuropsicología es una rama de la psicología que estudia la relación entre el sistema nervioso, las funciones cognitivas y el comportamiento. Este trabajo pretende describir el perfil de pacientes atendidos en la consulta de neuropsicología del Hospital Universitario La Paz (HULP) entre 2018 y 2023.

pmc-12565541.title: Clinical Phenotyping in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Steps Towards Personalized Medicine
pmc-12565541.creator: Paul Leon Petrick, Martin Mirus, Lars Heubner, Hani Harb, Mario Menk, Peter Markus Spieth
pmc-12565541.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a highly heterogeneous syndrome with a continuing high mortality rate. Despite intensive research, established therapies consist mainly of supportive measures, while pharmacological approaches have not yet shown any consistent survival benefits. In recent years, it has become clear that the great clinical and biological diversity of ARDS contributes significantly to the difficulty of demonstrating therapeutic effects. The phenotyping of ARDS has therefore become a central field of research.

pmc-12682499.title: An intelligent quantitative analysis software for videofluoroscopic swallowing study in patients with dysphagia
pmc-12682499.creator: Miao Wu, Fengmei Li, Chen Geng, Surong Qian, Yakang Dai, Tong Wang
pmc-12682499.description: BackgroundVideofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) employs quantitative analysis methods, which are valued in dysphagia diagnosis for their objectivity and precision. Nonetheless, conventional methods are laborious and time-consuming. Despite advancements in automatic tracking methods, existing software still requires substantial manual intervention and offers a restricted set of quantitative metrics.

pmc-13063619.title: Effect of family-centered empowerment model on self-efficacy of children with leukemia
pmc-13063619.creator: Omayma Mustafa Abu Samra, Sahar Farouk Hashem, Hend Wageh Abozed
pmc-13063619.description: Childhood leukemia is the most prevalent pediatric malignancy and remains a major contributor to childhood mortality, placing multiple burdens on affected families. Family engagement, a core element of the Family-Centered Empowerment Model (FCEM), aims to strengthen caregivers’ understanding of the disease, enhance their competencies, and improve children’s quality of life and self-efficacy (SE).

pmc-13471379.title: Graph Neural Networks and sequential architectures for autism detection from eye-tracking biomarkers: a multi-site study
pmc-13471379.creator: Nisrine El Ayat, Mohammed Boutalline, Adil Tannouche
pmc-13471379.description: BackgroundAutism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects 1 in 100 children globally, yet early detection remains challenging due to reliance on subjective behavioral assessments and limited specialist availability, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Eye-tracking biomarkers offer objective, quantitative measurements of visual attention patterns, but existing Neural Network approaches lack systematic evaluation across diverse neural network architectures and multi-site data.

pmc-13573451.title: Cleft Lip with or without palate in seven countries with two income levels: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13573451.creator: Rana A Alamoudi, Shahad N Abudawood, Fatma Dawood Abdulhameed, Eman Abdulbaset Alnamnakani, Sari M Rabah, Mustafa A Hamdan, Nasir H Alhamlan, Mohammad Zeinalddin, Ola B Al-Batayneh, Taimoor Al Bulushi, Mamdouh A AboulHassan, Mohamed Koraitim, Lateefa Alkharafi, Buthaina Almuqbali, Sultan Musaad Algh
pmc-13573451.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCleft lip with or without palate (CL/P) rank among the most prevalent congenital anomalies globally. This study aimed to report the phenotypic patterns of CL/P across seven Middle Eastern and Asian countries, reflecting two different economic levels.MethodologyA cross-sectional, multicountry-study was carried out in seven Middle Eastern and Asian countries (high income: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, UAE; lower-middle income: Egypt, Pakistan, Jordan) at major government and university cleft care referral centers.

pmc-13672310.creator: Marina Campos Rocha, Neta Shlezinger, Jean-Pierre Gangneux, Nicolas Papon
pmc-13672310.description: [2]. Echinocandins are recommended as first-line therapy for many types of invasive candidiasis, particularly candidemia in hospitalized patients [3].
